issues.legal_issue: The testimony of related witnesses is not rendered unreliable solely because disinterested neighbours who may have seen the occurrence were not examined.
material_facts: The witnesses who testified to the occurrence were related to, or interested in, the complainant.
The trial court and the High Court believed those witnesses.
The record did not show that anyone other than those witnesses had seen the occurrence.
The court noted that a co-accused’s petition for leave to appeal had been dismissed.
issues.conclusion: The non-examination of neighbours did not provide a reason to reject the testimony accepted by the trial court and the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the assessment of the evidence on the facts of the case: the witnesses’ relationship or interest and the non-examination of neighbours did not, in these circumstances, make their accepted testimony unreliable. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: appeal_against_criminal_conviction and related_witnesses_testified and lower_courts_credited_witnesses and no_other_eyewitnesses_identified and neighbours_not_examined

predicates.appeal_against_criminal_conviction: The accused appealed a criminal conviction.
predicates.related_witnesses_testified: Witnesses who were related to or interested in the complainant testified about the occurrence.
predicates.lower_courts_credited_witnesses: The trial court and the appellate court accepted the testimony of those witnesses.
predicates.no_other_eyewitnesses_identified: The record did not identify other people who had seen the occurrence.
predicates.neighbours_not_examined: Neighbours who may have seen the occurrence were not examined as witnesses.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a criminal conviction, related witnesses testified, the lower courts credited them, no other eyewitnesses were identified, and neighbours were not examined, the non-examination of those neighbours does not require rejection of the credible testimony.

issues.legal_issue: A participant who acts with a shared intention to murder is liable for the murder even when the shot fired at the intended victim strikes another person.
material_facts: The appellant and the shooter were on inimical terms with the intended victim.
After others began dragging the intended victim, the appellant urged the shooter to fire at him.
The shooter fired, but the shot struck the intended victim’s daughter, who later died.
The appellant again urged the shooter to fire at the intended victim and then aimed his own weapon at an intervening witness when the gun was taken from the shooter.
The trial court and the High Court found that the appellant shared the shooter’s intention to murder the intended victim.
issues.conclusion: The appellant’s acts established a common intention with the shooter to murder the intended victim, and the conviction for murder on that basis was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code. It held on the facts found by the lower courts that the appellant’s conduct went beyond merely shouting an exhortation and demonstrated a shared intention to commit murder. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: appeal_against_criminal_conviction and participant_urged_shooter_to_attack_intended_victim and participant_reinforced_attack_after_first_shot and participant_used_weapon_against_intervenor and shared_intent_to_murder_found

predicates.appeal_against_criminal_conviction: The accused appealed a criminal conviction.
predicates.participant_urged_shooter_to_attack_inte: The participant urged another person to shoot at the person they intended to attack.
predicates.participant_reinforced_attack_after_firs: After the first shot, the participant again urged the shooter to attack the intended victim.
predicates.participant_used_weapon_against_interven: The participant aimed or used a weapon against a person who intervened to stop the attack.
predicates.shared_intent_to_murder_found: The fact-finder found that the participant and shooter shared an intention to murder the intended victim.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a criminal conviction and the participant urged and reinforced an attack, used a weapon against an intervenor, and was found to share an intention to murder the intended victim, the participant is liable for murder committed in furtherance of that shared intention.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction under a provision imposing liability for common intention may replace a charge under a provision imposing liability for unlawful assembly when the facts and evidence are the same and the accused suffers no prejudice.
material_facts: The appellant had been charged with murder read with the provision concerning unlawful-assembly liability but was convicted of murder read with the provision concerning common intention.
The facts proved and the evidence adduced would have been the same had the appellant been charged on the basis of common intention.
The Court found no prejudice to the appellant from the substitution.
issues.conclusion: There was no illegality in convicting the appellant on the basis of common intention despite the charge having been framed on the basis of unlawful-assembly liability.
issues.legal_principle: Under Kannail Singh and Anr. v. The State of Punjab, (1954) SCR 904, the provisions concerning unlawful-assembly liability and common intention substantially differ but may overlap. Substitution is permissible when the facts to be proved and evidence to be adduced would be the same and the accused is not prejudiced; whether it is permissible depends on the facts of the case.

rule.if: appeal_against_criminal_conviction and charge_based_on_group_liability and conviction_based_on_common_intention and same_facts_and_evidence_apply and accused_not_prejudiced

predicates.appeal_against_criminal_conviction: The accused appealed a criminal conviction.
predicates.charge_based_on_group_liability: The accused was charged on a basis that attributed liability for an offence to participation in a group.
predicates.conviction_based_on_common_intention: The accused was convicted on a basis that attributed liability for an offence to a shared intention.
predicates.same_facts_and_evidence_apply: The facts to be proved and the evidence to be adduced would be the same under the charge and the basis of conviction.
predicates.accused_not_prejudiced: The change in the basis of liability did not prejudice the accused.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a criminal conviction, was charged on a group-liability basis, was convicted on a common-intention basis, the same facts and evidence apply, and the accused was not prejudiced, substituting the common-intention basis is not illegal.
